PARIS, Nov 8 : RC Lens' nightmare week continued as they conceded a late goal to lose 2-1 at home to Olympique de Marseille in Ligue 1 on Sunday after a humiliating 9-1 thrashing in the Champions League on Wednesday. Lens fell behind in the second minute when Amine Gouiri scored for Marseille, following a defensive error, but Florian Thauvin pulled them level in the 20th. They appeared on course to earn a point until Keyliane Abdallah struck with eight minutes remaining, the 20-year-old following up after Gouiri's initial effort was blocked, to condemn the hosts to a third successive defeat in all competitions. The defeat left Lens 11th in Ligue 1 and extended a miserable run that began when Olivier Giroud scored a late winner for Lille in last weekend's derby.

Wednesday's Champions League defeat to Como equalled the heaviest in the competition's history and marked another low for last season's Ligue 1 runners-up, whose fortunes have declined sharply since Pierre Sage left to take charge of Crystal Palace. His replacement Dino Toppmoeller lasted only a matter of weeks and Yannick Cahuzac's position is now also under scrutiny. Marseille, meanwhile, have climbed to fourth after overcoming their sluggish start to the campaign. They have won five successive Ligue 1 matches and also beat Bayer Leverkusen in the Europa League on Thursday. Earlier, Belgian defender Nathan Ngoy scored Lille's winner in a 2-1 victory at Rennes that lifted them to second. Lille have 21 points, two behind leaders Paris St Germain and one ahead of third-placed Paris FC. Marseille are fourth on 18 points, above Olympique Lyonnais, who lost 2-0 at Brest on Sunday. Nice continued their resurgence with a 2-0 win at Angers, their fourth victory in five league matches. Sofiane Diop opened the scoring in the second minute before Jonathan Clauss sealed the points in the 78th. The result lifted Nice to sixth, while Monaco slipped to seventh after conceding a 90th-minute equaliser in a 1-1 draw at promoted Le Mans. Monaco, beaten 3-1 by Paris FC last weekend, have gone five league matches without a win. Substitute Erwan Colas equalised from a corner to earn Le Mans a valuable point and lift them to 15th, outside the relegation zone.

(Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Toby Davis)

Source: Reuters

SYDNEY, Nov 9 : A senior Australian central banker said on Monday there was limited evidence that artificial intelligence had meaningfully lifted productivity and caused widespread job losses, but warned the technology could pose growing risks to financial stability. Speaking at a UBS conference in Sydney, Reserve Bank of Australia Assistant Governor Sarah Hunter judged the impact from AI on inflation would likely vary over time, initially boosting demand and adding to price pressures at a time when the economy was supply constrained. "Over time, supply will catch up with demand as data centre capacity and related sectors expand, easing current bottlenecks," she said. "If AI delivers broader productivity gains, economies will be able to produce more with the same inputs. As a result, the initial inflationary pressures from AI investment are likely to dissipate."

A boom in domestic data centre investment has added to demand pressures in the economy and is one reason the Reserve Bank of Australia has raised interest rates five times this year, taking them to an 18-year high of 4.85 per cent to fight inflation. Hunter said there was limited evidence AI has materially lifted productivity and that AI has had large effects on employment. "However, there are tentative signs of adjustment, through weaker job ad posting and employment outcomes in more AI-exposed occupations, and stronger growth in areas where the technology has had less of an impact, particularly for younger workers." She also warned of the possibility AI could increase risks to financial stability, with asset prices exposed to sharp repricing or even disorderly adjustments if AI investment returns fall short of expectations.

Source: Reuters

SAO PAULO, Nov 8 : Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies praised Isack Hadjar's performance at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix on Sunday, describing it as the driver's "best race" and another example of how he continues to raise the bar. The Frenchman finished third after starting fifth on the grid, securing a double podium for Red Bull alongside teammate Max Verstappen, who charged from 21st to second. "Ultimately, if you ask me right now, I think it's the best race he has done with us. In terms of pure pace," Mekies told reporters. "I think he has raised the bar all the time. So that's what we want to keep seeing." Hadjar, who recently signed a contract extension through 2027, has impressed in his first season with Red Bull, providing the consistent points haul the team has often lacked from its second car in recent years.

SAO PAULO, Nov 8 : Mercedes boss Toto Wolff may still be reluctant to compare Kimi Antonelli to Ayrton Senna but, after a week immersed in the late Brazilian driver's legacy and family, he suggested there may be room for a "Senninha" after all. Antonelli spent time with members of Senna's family ahead of Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix, sat in the cockpit of the triple world champion's 1986 Lotus and visited his grave before racing at Interlagos, where Senna remains a ubiquitous presence. The 20-year-old Italian became Formula One's youngest world champion after clinching the drivers' title in Mexico last week. While Wolff again cautioned against measuring Antonelli against the Brazilian great, he said members of the Senna family had jokingly embraced the Italian as a potential "Senninha", or "Little Senna".

"Comparing Kimi to Senna, I was always not very keen in having this comparison," Wolff told reporters. "Because, you know, Senna is a giant of the sport. Who he was as a person, who he was as a racing driver. "And I feel that setting these standards for a 20-year-old driver is a lot of pressure, and that's why I want to not compare him at that stage." But the Austrian struck a lighter tone when discussing Antonelli's reception in Brazil. "It's sweet to see how the Senna family embraces him. They say that it's the first time that it looks like there is a second Senninha. That is the first time that you can see, 'Okay, you know, he's a little bit like him'. "But maybe at that stage he's a Senninha and not a Senna yet. So let the Senninha develop, let him become a Senna." The remark carried particular resonance in Brazil, where "Senninha" is also the name of a hugely popular comic book character inspired by Senna and launched only months before the driver's death at Imola in 1994. Antonelli had spoken warmly to Reuters earlier in the week about Senna's influence on his career, describing the Brazilian as a childhood hero whose dedication, passion and empathy inspired him from an early age. The Italian's own Sao Paulo story, however, did not end with the fairy-tale victory many fans had hoped for. Starting strongly and taking the lead from second on the grid, Antonelli looked on course to win before spinning at Turn One, the famous Senna 'S'. He eventually finished fifth as McLaren's Lando Norris won the race. Mercedes, nevertheless, secured the constructors' championship. "I'm really disappointed for the race, and very angry to be fair," Antonelli told reporters. "But I'm going to put all this aside for now because the team clinched the title. "We were on for the win ... The spin came, which still is something I need to look at, because I don't know why I lost the rear so quickly," he added.

Source: Reuters

SYDNEY, Nov 9 : Cryptocurrencies fell sharply in late Sunday trade, with bitcoin and ether touching their lowest levels for more than two months, as investors fretted a Democratic Party-controlled US Congress will toughen regulation on the asset class. Bitcoin, the oldest and largest cryptocurrency by market capitalisation, fell by more than 2 per cent to $73,708, the lowest price since August. Ether fell about 5 per cent to $2,223, also the lowest since August. Crypto markets have been shaken in recent sessions by a $6 billion heist at Binance, the world's biggest exchange, and the election to office of high-profile critics in last week's US midterms.

MADRID, Nov 8 : Barcelona's Fermin Lopez scored twice as the visitors came from behind to win 2-1 at Atletico Madrid and retain a three-point lead at the top of LaLiga on Sunday. Barca's win takes them clear of second-placed Real Madrid, who moved to 30 points with a 3-0 win at lowly Valencia on Saturday, and five ahead of Atletico in third after 12 games. The hosts imposed a tempo that Barcelona struggled to counteract before the break. In the second half, the Catalans had a firm grip and the momentum, as coach Hansi Flick's typically aggressive side showed they could exert control too. Atletico began much stronger, though, piercing Barca's high defensive line with ease. Both sides hit the bar in the opening eight minutes, but it was the home team who deservedly opened the scoring after 10 minutes.

Julian Alvarez had already passed up a golden opportunity, but provided the cross for Giuliano Simeone to bundle the ball into the net from close range. Atletico coach Diego Simeone had every reason to be pleased with his side's performance when he asked for calm in the 28th minute. The only disappointment was that their smart attacking play had not yielded another goal. "Of course we wish Julian was as clinical as he normally is, but we're going to wait for Julian (to get back to his best) because he's a great player," Simeone told reporters. "In order to get where we want to go, we need a great Julian. And if not, we won't get there." As the half went on, Barca gradually found ways to hurt Atletico, primarily through Lamine Yamal and Pedri. The latter's driving run led to Fermin sweeping a loose ball into the corner for the equaliser in the 45th minute. Barcelona dominated proceedings after the break and Atletico's forays into the opposition half became rare.  "We were too far from the opponent, so it was not easy to get pressure on the ball," Flick said of Barcelona's first-half display. "This was what we did better in the second half. The first was not so perfect, but the second was good and I think we deserved the win." When Lamine finally conjured a clear chance with an incisive pass, Fermin provided a clinical finish in the 66th. On the touchline, Simeone desperately pleaded with his side to mount a final onslaught with 10 minutes remaining, but Barca choked the life out of the game with slick possession. Elsewhere, late goals from Real Betis' Rodrigo Riquelme and Marc Bartra maintained their side's grip on fourth spot following a 2-0 win at Elche, who go into the international break in the relegation zone as a result. Real Sociedad lie four points behind Betis in fifth after Orri Oskarsson's second-half goal gave his side a 1-0 home win over Rayo Vallecano. Villarreal beat visitors Getafe 2-0 and Levante held out for a 0-0 draw at Celta Vigo.

Source: Reuters

SAO PAULO, Nov 8 : Lando Norris emerged unscathed from an eventful Sao Paulo Grand Prix podium celebration on Sunday after smashing a champagne bottle and appearing to get an unexpected blast from fireworks moments after winning the race. The McLaren driver, who won from pole position at Interlagos for the second year in a row, broke his champagne bottle as he attempted his trademark celebration of banging it against the podium floor to pop the cork. The Briton then appeared startled when pyrotechnics ignited nearby during the celebrations, television footage showed, prompting concern on social media that he may have been burned. McLaren team principal Andrea Stella said afterwards that Norris was "all right".

"I have not talked to him, I have not checked. I understand he is all right," the Italian told reporters. "I understand that he had an incident with the pyrotechnic, not with the bottle. I think that the bottle didn't go well either, because it seemed like it had only the upper part. "But I think he was just surprised that when he was going for the bottle I understand that the pyrotechnic started." The podium drama came after a dominant drive from Norris in mixed conditions, with the 26-year-old adding to his victories in Hungary and the Netherlands this season. Stella was full of praise for the 2025 world champion, highlighting his ability to excel when conditions are changing. "When Lando operates at his best, he is definitely one of the best drivers on the grid," he said. "We have seen that in these conditions, like yesterday, it is not the first time that when you have mixed, variable conditions, he kind of is one of the fastest in finding the limit, and you have seen it today as well, when the track was in the middle between dry and wet." While Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli has already clinched the drivers' championship, Norris is sixth overall, 33 points behind second-placed Max Verstappen. Mercedes secured the constructors' title at Interlagos.

JERUSALEM: Former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot said on Sunday (Nov 8) he will work to form a wide government as quickly as possible, but his path to power was uncertain following a deadlocked election that failed to dislodge Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Saturday gave Eisenkot the first opportunity to try to form a new government after the Oct 27 election left both Eisenkot and Netanyahu short of the majority needed to govern. Herzog officially handed Eisenkot the task on Sunday at a meeting at the president's residence, starting the clock on what Eisenkot said would be an "extraordinarily complex" process. "We are in a state of emergency, approaching a point of no return for the State of Israel," Eisenkot said. "We must form a national emergency government. This will require creative and unconventional political steps."

Eisenkot said Israeli democracy was at a vulnerable moment at a time when it faced immense challenges, with Herzog citing a threat of attack from Iran, the need to progress towards peace in Gaza and negotiations with Lebanon and other neighbours. "There is great urgency for new leadership, leadership that people can look in the eye and trust," Eisenkot said. His potential pathways to power include trying to form a minority government with Arab party support for key issues; forming a coalition with ultra-Orthodox parties that he and his allies have shunned in the past; or forging a unity government with Netanyahu. All three options face formidable obstacles.

Related:

Israel faces new era of sinking US support after election

Netanyahu rivals seize on Democrats' sweep of US Congress, seeking his ouster

NEGOTIATIONS COULD TAKE SIX WEEKS Eisenkot said he will call on all parties to join who meet his main principles. These include recognition of Israel as a Jewish and democratic state; a duty of national service for all to strengthen the military and expand its ranks; and recognition of Hamas as a terrorist organisation and a commitment to destroying its military and governing capacity. "I am convinced that it is possible and right to form a new government quickly, one that will win a large majority in the Knesset," Eisenkot said, referring to Israel's parliament. Eisenkot now has 28 days plus a possible 14-day extension. If he fails, Netanyahu will likely get his shot at forming a government. Should he also be unable, new elections could be called. Herzog, who consulted with all parties, said Eisenkot received the "clear and unequivocal support" of a majority of lawmakers on who has the better chance of forming the next government that will win the confidence of the Knesset. Netanyahu's Likud won the most seats of any single party with 27 in the 120-seat Knesset, but Netanyahu's wider religious-nationalist coalition garnered only 53 in total, short of a 61-seat majority in the 120-seat parliament.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, casts his ballot in his Likud party primary elections ahead of Israel's general election in October, in Jerusalem, Aug 17, 2026. (Photo: AP/Ohad Zwigenberg)

Eisenkot's Yashar party emerged as the second-largest party with 21 seats, while his coalition, spanning four centre-left to right-wing Jewish-led parties, won just 48 seats. Two parties representing Israel's Arab minority won an unprecedented 19 seats. Netanyahu called for a unity government of all Zionist parties to preserve a Jewish state, while giving no indication whether he would was prepared to serve under Eisekenkot's leadership. "This is the will of the people and the need of the hour," he said in a statement, ruling out a coalition government with Arabs, who make up 21 per cent of Israel's population. Potentially making Eisenkot's job tougher is the position of one opposition leader, Avigdor Lieberman of the Israel Our Home party, who has ruled out a unity government with Netanyahu or a minority government that has backing from Arab parties. But Lieberman has softened his stance on sitting with ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties as long as they agree to support a law under which ultra-Orthodox men serve in the military. "Given the current reality, in order to prevent further elections and bring an end to the Netanyahu era, there is no choice but to make difficult decisions and resolve issues where flexibility is possible and common ground can be found," Lieberman said.

Source: Reuters/fs

Both the US and Iran have continued strikes on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, however, restricting exports of energy and other commodities vital to the world economy.

WASHINGTON/CAIRO: US President Donald Trump on Sunday (Nov 8) said he was highly unlikely to order fresh attacks on Iran as long as talks to end the conflict progress , even as both countries reported that shipping had been hit in or near the Strait of Hormuz. "It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement," Trump told CNN in a phone interview. "The answer is, highly unlikely it's going to be necessary." CNN did not specify exactly what it had asked Trump, who also said that if strikes resume, the US has identified potential infrastructure targets, including 38 bridges "that we can knock down in literally one hour". Trump had hinted at renewing major attacks on Iran after last week's US midterm elections, but there has been no sign of a large-scale US military operation. Iran has said it would respond by striking US and Israeli targets.

Iran ian media suggested that explosions in southern Iran on Saturday were related to Iran ian military activities rather than US strikes. Iran 's state television said officials had not confirmed any missile strikes on Iran ian territory following blasts heard in several areas, including on Qeshm Island in the strait. Both the US and Iran have continued strikes on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, however, restricting exports of energy and other commodities vital to the world economy. Iran 's state television said the evening explosions might be related to Iran ian military activity in the waterway, where Iran said two vessels had hit mines and a third had caught fire.

Related:

Iran says forces 'stronger' than at beginning of war

The US said its air force had disabled a vessel in the Gulf of Oman beyond the strait. Tasnim news agency said two missiles had struck Qeshm Island, with no official information on possible damage. Neither Iran nor the US has commented on that report. Washington said on Nov 2 that it had struck the island in a limited defensive measure against Iran ians using surface-to-air missiles against US assets. COMMERCIAL VESSEL, OIL TANKERS HIT Since the US and Israel began attacks on Iran in February, Tehran has sought the upper hand by hitting vessels in the Strait of Hormuz to block Gulf energy exports, while US forces began blockading movements to and from Iran ian ports in April. The US military said on Saturday evening that its air force had fired at the stern of a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman, disabling it as it tried to get through the blockade. Iran 's Revolutionary Guards Navy said two oil tankers had caught fire after hitting mines while attempting to pass through an "unauthorised route" in the Strait of Hormuz. A third tanker had also suffered an explosion and caught fire, the semi-official Fars news agency reported later. Reuters was not able to confirm any of the reported strikes. Monitors from the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said a bulk carrier and military forces were involved in an incident in the Gulf of Oman, approximately 18 nautical miles east of the United Arab Emirates' city of Khor Fakkan, with damage unknown. It was unclear if it was related to the reported US attack.

Smoke rises from the stern of a St. Kitts-flagged cargo vessel following what US Central Command says was a strike on Saturday to disable the vessel, which was trying to break the US blockade of Iran, at a location given as the Gulf of Oman, in this still image taken from video released Nov 7, 2026. (Photo: Handout via REUTERS/US Central Command)

SAUDI STATE OIL COMPANY BUILDING DAMAGED A conflict between Iran -aligned Houthis in Yemen and Saudi Arabia has escalated this month, enlarging the wider Middle East war. On Sunday, Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said an administrative building belonging to state oil company Saudi Aramco in Riyadh had been damaged by falling debris after an attempted attack, with no injuries or fatalities reported. Qatar, which has been mediating in talks to try to end the conflict that has shaken the world economy, on Saturday denied reports that the US and Iran had failed to reach a deal. The Qatari prime minister had affirmed that both sides were continuing to work toward an agreement, it said. Iran has submitted a nuclear proposal to Washington through Qatar, a senior Iran ian official told Reuters on Thursday, saying the US was reviewing it but discussions would depend on Washington first meeting Tehran's seven demands. These include sanctions relief, access to frozen assets and war reparations, while Washington insists nuclear issues must feature in initial talks. On Saturday, the US military said it was launching a task force to crack down on the movement of advanced weapons and other sanctioned material to Iran via its land borders and the Caspian Sea — part of economic measures to try to pressure Tehran. Iran 's Revolutionary Guards dismissed the plan as "wordplay", saying it would not work because Tehran had made preparations and communicated closely with its neighbours.

Nov 8 : Freiburg have never finished higher than third place in the Bundesliga but their flying start to the season has raised hopes of a record campaign after Sunday's 2-0 home win over Union Berlin. An own goal from Rani Khedira and a strike by Yuito Suzuki handed Freiburg a victory that leaves them in third place, two points behind leaders Bayern Munich. Freiburg's best season came in 1994/95 when they finished third under their long-serving coach Volker Finke. They have been close to repeating that in recent years, finishing in the top seven in four of the last five seasons, but there is growing belief they can go further under current coach Julian Schuster.

"We had to be very patient and yet we remained very confident. We didn't have many opportunities, but we allowed very little ourselves,” Schuster said of the win over Union. Union coach Mauro Lustrinelli praised Freiburg's attractive style before the match and said it was something he wanted his side to emulate. Their improved goalscoring this campaign has been behind their strong start.  With 20 goals, they are averaging 2.22 goals per game this season, up from 1.50 last term, with only Bayern, on 29 goals, and RB Leipzig, on 27, having scored more. It is often said a coach needs three seasons to really bed in his ideas at a club and build a squad, and Schuster is now in his third campaign having been appointed in July 2024. Freiburg are away to promoted Elversberg after the international break, looking to build on a run of four straight wins in all competitions. Bayer Leverkusen rose to fifth thanks to a 2-1 win at Cologne in the Rhine derby. Aleix Garcia and Patrik Schick put Leverkusen 2-0 up before the home side made it a tense finish when Said El Mala scored in added time. Hoffenheim climbed to ninth after goals from Fisnik Asllani and Tim Lemperle gave them a 2-1 home win over second-bottom Schalke.

NEW YORK, Nov 8 : American Bryson DeChambeau said on Sunday he would face the next chapter of his career with "humility and respect", days after LIV Golf announced plans to liquidate. LIV Golf's financing plan collapsed this week and the circuit said it would wind down operations after the Saudi Public Investment Fund announced it would cut funding. BC Partners has revived efforts to create a successor, the Financial Times reported on Sunday. DeChambeau's choice to leave the PGA Tour for the Saudi-backed circuit four years ago marked one of the highest-profile defections in an acrimonious, multiyear saga that engulfed the sport.

"I'm not going to rewrite the last four years. I made a decision I believed in, and I'm grateful for what came with it: playing in front of fans new and old around the world who rarely got to see the best players at home," DeChambeau said on social media. "I believed this game could reach more people, in more places, in a new way. I still believe that. And I gave it everything I had to keep team golf alive." Former major champions including Jon Rahm, Brooks Koepka and Patrick Reed had already signalled their departure from LIV. Koepka was reinstated by the PGA Tour under its "Returning Member Program." But many LIV players, who were lured to the breakaway circuit by supersized paychecks, face an awkward and challenging return to established tours. "Arnold Palmer said no player is bigger than the game, and I want to acknowledge that, along the way, I've said some things that didn't help," said DeChambeau, who plans to compete at Gary Player's Nedbank Golf Challenge in December. "Whatever comes next, I'll approach it with humility and respect for the people who carried this game before me."

Nvidia said on Sunday (Nov 8) it is probing whether CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, after a media report alleged he had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to Beijing. Huang sa id in a message to employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife and took "full responsibility" for his actions, while Nvidia said the CEO was committed to continuing to lead the company without interruption. The developments are likely to pressure the chipmaker's stock, which has already seen sharp declines recently amid worries about AI sustainability, and may also raise questions about Huang's future at the helm of the company he co-founded . The New York Times reported last month that Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based company Megaspeed, whom US authorities investigated and concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset.

US authorities have scrutinised Megaspeed, which buys AI chips from Nvidia , over suspicions it helped Beijing gain access to advanced AI chips that are barred from shipment to China. "The Nvidia Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation," Nvidia said. The company said on Sunday that, while its board has no reason to believe that either US national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, its inquiry will examine all available information. Huang fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it, it added. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio declined to comment on Huang when asked by reporters on Sunday evening.

Related:

Nvidia chips pile up in Hong Kong as China withholds import approval

Trump says US looking ‘closely’ at report Nvidia CEO is target of China spy plot

PILING PRESSURE ON NVIDIA The investigation adds to pressure on Nvidia at a time investors are already pulling back from uncertainty over the sustainability of the AI market, in which the company is a leader. The US$4.5 trillion chipmaker's shares have given up all their gains this year amid a broader tech market rout triggered by worries over AI sustainability. "There is clearly risk that Jensen could be removed as CEO depending on the Board investigation and this will add risk to the stock as he is so important to the Nvidia story and strategy globally," said Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co. "This is a black eye moment for Jensen and will spark multiple congressional inquiries at a minimum and will create an overhang on the stock," Ives said, adding that the news would also increase major scrutiny about selling chips to China. Huang admitted to having been unfaithful to his wife, saying, "My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry." Addressing his colleagues, board, partners and shareholders, Huang said: "My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to Nvidia and will work to earn back your confidence." Top Republican lawmakers in the US House of Representatives have already called on Huang to brief Congress this month about the New York Times report . The report raises "significant national security concerns regarding (China's) access to sensitive US technology and information", the lawmakers said in a letter dated November 4.  "It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which US national security has been placed at risk," they added. US export controls since 2022 have sought to restrict China's access to advanced Nvidia chips and the equipment needed to make them. Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993, said that he was "committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security". Nvidia had earlier said that Huang talks with "thousands of customer executives every year", and that cloud customers in Asia receive ordinary business information, not sensitive Nvidia trade secrets or anything tied to US national security.

Source: Reuters/fs/bg
